column1: # STEPS.tsv -- THE DESIGN-PLAN fleet-queue STEP TABLE (the cio, 2026-11-05, on Lon's word in the cio's window, verbatim: "Time to design a better system. We have 2 Fable 5.1, 1 Opus 5.5 xhigh, 4 Opus 5.5 high, 4 Sonnet 5.5 xhigh, and 20 Haiku 5.5 xhigh. We want each level in the hierarchy serving the one below. On the CxO have designated roles. company men and workers can do anything given the proper SKILL FIRST. We want a queueing in the system and an escalation in the system." / "Take the design from yesterday, take the good parts. Mainly learn from the industry and use suggested and proven tools for all aspects." / 16:30 to the coo: "How about a N x N x N x N system of Fable x Opus x Sonnet x Haiku. Such that any available senior can take any seats help if their queue is small. Use a queueing system. That was NO BOTTLENECKS."). The design text is skill fleet-bus section 8; the industry grounding is skill fleet-ops-industry.

# harness/scripts/test_design_fleet_queue_steps.sh reads it: --list prints it; --step N runs the step's probe (column 5, one bash command run from S4E_HOME with a 600 s budget): rc 0 GREEN, rc 1 RED, rc 2 could not measure. Every probe reads a live mechanism, a unit, a tube or a ledger the step builds; a step reads RED until its mechanism exists and GREEN only while the fleet meets it; no probe is satisfied by a deletion.

# THE PROVEN TOOLS under the plan (one per aspect, never a hand-rolled copy): beanstalkd 1.12 (apt; tubes, priorities, reserve, TTR leases, touch, bury, kick, delay, binlog) for the queue, the leases and the dead letters; greenstalk (pip) as its client; systemd --user timer and service units for the tick and the daemons; flock (util-linux) for the bus lock; GNU sem (parallel, apt) for the compile and run pools; cgroup v2 through systemd-run and systemd-oomd for the box (box-scheduler steps 1-7 kept); SQLite 3.45 for the outcome ledger; git worktree, s4e_land.sh and a git merge driver for the repo (box-scheduler 18-19 kept).

# PHASE A (built before the fleet fires, by the cio and the coo, under Lon's one apt line): steps 1-7, 10-12, 16, 18, 19. PHASE B (built by the fleet as jobs in the tubes): 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 17, and box-scheduler's open steps 13, 19, 20, 24, 25, 27, 30, 34, 36.
